## Findings

### 1. MEDIUM — the `running` early return suppresses the retry for `undelivered` threads
`packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2837-2841` (`notifyMember`, not `notifyMemberAtWake` as the brief said).

The guard is `cause.kind === 'running' && delivery?.covered !== undefined && delivery.covered !== ''`. `covered` is `plan.delivered` from `coverInboxFacts`/`beginInboxDelivery` (`index.ts:3305-3317`), and by construction `delivered` **deliberately excludes threads the notice could not render** (`inbox-delivery.ts:70-78`: `if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push(...)`).

Concrete trace: a single commit mentions member M in 9 Threads. `notificationText` caps rendered scopes at 8 (`index.ts:3169-3177`) and returns `undelivered = [T9]` (`index.ts:3211`). `beginInboxDelivery` records `covered = signature(T1..T8)` — **non-empty** — plus `undelivered: [T9]`. Under the old code, when M's own turn starts the `agent/status → 'running'` edge runs `deliverInboxNotice`, `inboxDeliveryPlan` sees `plan.signature` (includes T9) ≠ `covered` → `trigger === 'immediate'` → T9 is re-attempted. With the early return, the `running` edge returns before `deliverInboxNotice`: `covered !== ''` is true, so T9's facts wait for the next commit/activation touching M.

Impact: M's direct mention in T9 is durably unread but is not re-attempted on the member's own next run edge. No data loss (the facts rederive on the next commit), but the retry surface documented in `inbox-delivery.ts` ("an unchanged rederivation still sees them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down") is narrowed to commit/activation causes only. Consistent with the coordinator's finding that removing the block changes no test outcome — no test covers the `undelivered` retry.
Smallest fix: add `&& delivery.undelivered.length === 0` to the guard (or replace the block with `plan.trigger === undefined`, which is exactly the dedup below and makes the new block redundant).

### 2. LOW — "coverage non-empty" is a weaker test than the dedup it pre-empts
Same block. The existing dedup (`index.ts:2899`) compares the *full* signature against `covered`; the new guard short-circuits before that comparison exists. Any future state where `covered` is stale-but-non-empty (a commit whose notice was skipped — e.g. `notifyMember` returning at the `member.state !== 'enabled'` check at 2830-2833 — while new facts accumulated) now skips a read that the old code would have turned into a delivery. I traced every such path I could find (`state !== enabled`, transition in flight, deferred effect skipped at shutdown, `dropInboxCoverage` on failure) and each is followed by an activation/transition/commit cause that re-delivers, which is why I rate this LOW rather than a live bug.

### 3. LOW — the read set is instance state that assumes a synchronous read
`packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts` (`notificationReadSet` field, `withNotificationReadSet`, `unreadFor`, `mainUnreadForNotification`). The cache is only sound because no `await` exists between set and `finally` restore, and ledger mutation happens only inside enqueued operation bodies (`enqueue`/`operationTail`, `ledger.ts:6619`). Correct today; a future `await` inside any of these reads silently turns the cache into cross-task staleness. Informational in nature, worth a one-line constraint comment.

### 4. LOW — benchmark counter is mislabelled
`scripts/team-performance/team-performance-baseline.ts:649-651`: the wrapper increments `notificationTextMissingPlan` when `args[3] === undefined`, but in the new signature `(agent, notifications, readerId, main, deliveryPlan, prefix)` index 3 is `main`, not the delivery plan. The counter measures "empty Main list", not "missing plan", so before/after comparisons that read it are misleading.

### 5. LOW — fixture assertions that omit the location
`packages/agent-team/tests/check-package-boundaries.spec.ts`: four cases assert only `toMatchObject({ code: 1 })` with no line/file assertion, so a checker that rejects at the wrong line still passes. Also `.cts` and `import x = require('…')` are not covered (see A/F below for why the latter is only theoretical).

## Candidate concerns rejected

- **A (parameter order) — rejected.** Exactly two call sites in `src`: `index.ts:1326` `(handle.agent, notifications, member.memberId, mainNotifications, undefined, text)` and `index.ts:2915` `(…, plan)`. The only other caller is the benchmark wrapper, which forwards `...args` unchanged. `lib/index.js:1279/2832` is the stale compiled copy (gitignored build output).
- **B (reentrancy) — rejected.** `withNotificationReadSet` saves `previous` and restores it in `finally`; a nested call for a different memberId builds its own set and restores the outer one on exit; a nested call for the *same* memberId returns `read()` with no set swap, which is the intended reuse. Nothing captures the cached arrays into a longer-lived structure: both entry points (`notificationFacts`, `notificationSnapshot`) return only frozen arrays built inside the callback, and the cached values are already-frozen `unreadForFrom` results.
- **C (stale cache) — rejected.** Both entry points are fully synchronous, and ledger writes only occur inside `enqueue`'s awaited bodies, so no commit can interleave with a read. Also a genuine improvement in this change: `notificationText` now receives the caller's `plan` instead of recomputing it without `previous` (`index.ts:3042`), so the notice and the recorded coverage agree and the duplicate `inboxDeliveryPlan` pass is gone.
- **D(i) shutdown — rejected.** `accepting = false` is set synchronously at the top of the dispose effect (`index.ts:757`), before any queued `setImmediate` can run, so every queued effect sees `false`. Measured `ranAfterShutdownRequest: 0`.
- **D(ii) hang — rejected.** The `try/catch/finally` sits *inside* the `setImmediate` callback, so a throwing `effect()` is caught and `resolve()` runs in `finally`; even a throwing `logger.warn` still runs `finally { resolve() }` before escaping the callback. Every `queued` settles, so `await team.notificationEffectTail` is a real drain.
- **D(iii) premature tail resolution — rejected.** Deletion is guarded by `this.notificationEffectTails.get(id) === queued`, so only the newest chain for a member ever deletes, and `notificationEffectTail` is recomputed on every map mutation. A same-member chain-3 arriving after chain-2 settled makes chain-2's cleanup see the mismatch and skip deletion, and the recomputation already includes chain-3. Nothing is dropped from the aggregate.
- **E (new suppressible state) — partially confirmed, see finding 1.** The guard *is* reachable in states where the existing dedup would not have returned, and finding 1 gives the concrete case.
- **F — mostly clean.** (i) The AST walk classifies correctly: `import type {X}` / `export type {X}` (clause `isTypeOnly`), `import {type X}` and `import type * as ns` (all specifiers type-only) are exempt; `import {X, type Y}` is a real reference (default/namespace bindings return `false` early); bare `import '…'`, `export * from`, `export {X} from` and dynamic `import('…')` are recorded; comments and quoted strings can no longer match, which the fixture proves. Unwalked and worth noting: `import x = require('…')` (ImportEqualsDeclaration) would be a false negative — but the tree is ESM with no such usage. (ii) Widening `SOURCE_PATTERN` changes nothing in this repo: the only `.mts`/`.cts` files are three `.d.mts` under `scripts/`, outside `packages/*/src`; `check:boundaries` still reports 112 files and passes (verified post-15:39). (iii) `typescript` is a root **devDependency** (`^5.8.3`, resolved here as 5.9.3) and the script runs from the root; it never ships (`files` only lists `packages/*/lib`), so this is fine — it would only fail under `--omit=dev`, which no workflow uses. (iv) The fixture's 10 cases are well chosen and the "N source file(s) in M package(s)" assertions prove `--root` is honoured rather than the real repo being scanned; the gaps are listed as finding 5.
- **G (tautology) — rejected.** The deferral defers to `setImmediate`, which cannot run between an `await` continuation and the next statement, so `toEqual([])` right after `await startThread` is deterministic, and the coordinator's mutation probe (deferral off → 8 calls at that assertion) confirms it is load-bearing. Gap worth noting: the test uses exactly 8 members, so it covers the threshold boundary but nothing asserts the sub-threshold path still delivers synchronously, and nothing covers two commits for the same member ordering.
